segments.title: Chương 45: 0045 [Tiêu diệt Nǎo Bái Jīn]
segments.content:
Evening self-study hadn't started yet, and the students were a little excited today.

When they came back from the weekend break, they found a television had been installed in the classroom!

Everyone had one of these at home, but having one installed in the classroom was a rare sight.

Someone ran over to turn on the TV, and everyone lost the mood to do practice problems. Even the top students were watching with great interest.

The whole class watched a cartoon together.

"It's him, it's him, it's him, it's really him. Our friend, little Nezha..."

When the ending song played, many students sang along.

Some even deliberately sang "Nezha" in a local dialect that sounded like "na zhua," making the other students roar with laughter.

This cartoon had premiered this summer, with only the first 26 episodes produced at the time. Now, they were finally airing the episodes after the 26th.

They kept watching until it was almost time for evening self-study, when their homeroom teacher, Liu Shuying, suddenly appeared. It was too late for the students to turn off the TV.

"Slap! Slap!"

Liu Shuying picked up a teaching pointer made of mottled bamboo and smacked it twice on the lectern. "The televisions were installed by the school for everyone. They can only receive the CCTV General Channel. I won't stop you from watching programs, but you're only allowed to watch 'Legal Report' after lunch. And you have to turn the volume down so you don't disturb other students."

"Yeah!"

"Whoa~~~"

The whole class cheered. Their dull and tedious senior year of high school finally had a recreational activity.

Yes, "Legal Report" could also be an entertainment program!

"Quiet, quiet!"

Liu Shuying continued to rap the pointer. "The monthly exam is the weekend after next, to test how your review is coming along. The exam questions will mainly be based on the review material, but will also cover knowledge points from all of high school. This is the last monthly exam of 2003, and I hope everyone will take it seriously."

With that, she sat down on the platform and announced the start of evening self-study.

The class monitor, Li Rui, quickly went to turn off the television.

Chen Guiliang took out his math practice worksheet and started working on it earnestly. When he got stuck, he would flip through his textbook and notes. If he still couldn't figure it out, he would circle the problem and ask the top students after class.

This was especially true for the more complex problems, which required the comprehensive application of many knowledge points, some of which Chen Guiliang hadn't reviewed yet.

After enduring the first session of evening self-study, the homeroom teacher, Liu Shuying, got up and left.

Xie Yang ran over and whispered, "Great Hero Chen, hurry and call Boss Tao. Ask him what's happening tonight."

Chen Guiliang smiled. "Weren't you going to study hard for the college entrance exam?"

"The two aren't mutually exclusive," Xie Yang said.

Chen Guiliang left the classroom and headed for the rooftop. The door to the rooftop stairwell was locked, but it had long since been pried open by someone.

Dialing the number, Chen Guiliang asked, "Brother Gang, has the attack on Sabac started?"

"Hahaha, that's hilarious," Tao Chenggang started laughing as soon as he spoke. "The other guilds aren't even trying to take Sabac. Instead, they've all teamed up to gank Boss Shi. Boss Shi's guild may have the most players, the highest levels, and the best gear, but they've been killed and forced back to the safe zone by the combined forces of several major guilds."

Chen Guiliang asked, "How did he piss everyone off?"

Tao Chenggang said, "His identity got exposed. The major guilds have been spamming 'Kill Nao Baijin.' Even solo players who aren't in a guild are running over to help when they hear the slogan. I even sent Boss Shi a QQ message to explain that I wasn't the one who leaked his identity."

"What's the situation now?" Chen Guiliang pressed.

Tao Chenggang said, "The members of Boss Shi's guild don't even dare to leave the safe zone now, and some have even quit the guild. Boss Shi's Void Judgment also dropped, and now he's leading a bunch of his lackeys in a flame war with the other players."

"This must be affecting President Shi's gaming experience. He's not going to just quit in a fit of anger, is he?" Chen Guiliang was afraid the whale would leave.

"Hold on, he just sent me a QQ message."

Tao Chenggang stopped talking for two or three minutes, then continued, "Boss Shi plans to go all in. He's going to openly reveal his identity and keep fighting. He wants me to change his ID to 'The Only Gift I Accept is Nao Baijin.' He's recharged another 3,000 yuan, says he can't be bothered with attacking Sabac anymore, and wants to farm full Abyss Zuma sets for his core guild members first."

"Then change his name. We have to serve our customer well," Chen Guiliang said cheerfully.

Boss Shi was currently cursing people out. He had already figured out that his identity had been exposed by one of his hired levelers.

This leveler had bragged in the game before, showing off that he was President Shi's gaming secretary. Many veteran players on the same server knew him.

But Boss Shi only cursed a few lines and soon led his underlings to farm the Abyss Zuma instance.

His overpowered weapon, "Void Judgment," had just been dropped when he was killed. He had to get another one.

Once he had farmed enough Abyss Zuma, he would go to higher-level maps to run instances.

In the next battle for Sabac, he would be able to crush them with superior gear.

Right, the Woma and Zuma instances only required one entry ticket.

But higher-level instance maps required two or three tickets. Without deep pockets, you really wouldn't dare to farm them repeatedly!

After relaying what happened in the game, Xie Yang burst out laughing, wishing he could go and land a few blows on Boss Shi himself.

Back in the classroom, Chen Guiliang took his math practice worksheet and went to ask a top student, Wu Meng, for help.

He also took the opportunity to chat with Bian Guanyue for a bit.

"Wu Meng, I can't solve this problem. Can you help explain it?" Chen Guiliang walked over and squatted down.

Wu Meng had finished this worksheet long ago. She immediately picked up a pen and said, "First, establish a coordinate system and determine the coordinates of the four points A, B, C, and D. Then, based on the given conditions, find the equations for the two lines OF and GE. Combine the two equations to find the parametric equations related to point P. Then, eliminate the parameter to get the locus equation of point P..."

Chen Guiliang listened attentively. Whenever he didn't understand something, he would write down the knowledge point. It was all content he hadn't reviewed yet.

After asking about two complex problems in a row, Chen Guiliang said, "Thank you."

"You're welcome." Wu Meng blushed and lowered her head.

It wasn't because Chen Guiliang was too handsome, but because she blushed whenever she spoke to any member of the opposite sex.

Still squatting, Chen Guiliang winked at Bian Guanyue. "How was your weekend?"

"Reading and doing practice problems at home," Bian Guanyue said.

Chen Guiliang said shamelessly, "I'm craving spicy potatoes. Can you bring me some tomorrow?"

Bian Guanyue asked, "What spice level do you want?"

"Regular spicy is fine," Chen Guiliang said.

"Okay."

Bian Guanyue agreed, then said no more, silently burying her head in her practice problems.

Chen Guiliang returned to his seat with his math worksheet and took out an English worksheet to continue working.

Zheng Feng was a little anxious, wanting to know what Chen Guiliang and Bian Guanyue had just talked about.

Li Jun was sprawled on his desk, fast asleep, and would probably sleep until the end of evening self-study.

Guan Zhiqiang was still reading a novel, drool unconsciously trickling from his mouth again.

After working on her problems for a while, Wu Meng finally couldn't help but ask, "Are you dating Chen Guiliang?"

"No," Bian Guanyue replied.

Wu Meng said, "Then why are you bringing him potatoes?"

Bian Guanyue said, "He's a good friend of mine."

Wu Meng wasn't usually very talkative, but she got along well with Bian Guanyue. She glanced around furtively and whispered, "Don't you think Chen Guiliang has gotten more handsome?"

"He changed his clothes and hairstyle. It's been several days now."

Bian Guanyue was very satisfied with her aesthetic sense. She had picked out those clothes, and she was the one who took Chen Guiliang to get that haircut.

Wu Meng asked, "Have you ever been in a relationship?"

"No," Bian Guanyue shook her head, then smiled. "You want to?"

Wu Meng quickly denied it. "I want to get into Peking University. I'll date when I'm there. Strolling with my boyfriend by Weiming Lake must be so romantic."

Bian Guanyue sighed. "Sigh, I'll be lucky to get into a Tier 2 university."

Wu Meng asked curiously, "But you learn so fast. It doesn't seem like you'd only be able to get into a Tier 3 school."

"I used to be an arts student. When I was little, I learned to sing traditional opera from my grandparents. Because there's no future in traditional opera, I started studying vocal music in middle school," Bian Guanyue explained simply.

Wu Meng said, "Then you don't have to worry about the college entrance exam. Your academic scores are good enough for a Tier 3 university, which is already amazing for an arts student."

"I don't want to be an arts student anymore," Bian Guanyue said. "The arts exams are coming up soon, and I haven't registered for a single school. I'm going to rely on my own ability to get into a proper university, to show certain people!"

"You're so brave, switching to a regular student track in your senior year," Wu Meng said with admiration.

Bian Guanyue said, "That's why I have to work twice as hard and catch up on all the knowledge I've missed. My goal is to get into a mid-ranked Tier 2 university."

"You can do it!"

"You too. I hope you get into Peking University."

While these two girls were striving hard, Chen Guiliang's new deskmate, Qin Shanshan, was in a daze.

She was slumped over her desk, doing nothing. She couldn't focus on reading, nor did she have any interest in doing practice problems.

Aversion to studying.

Actually, Qin Shanshan used to have pretty good grades.

"Hey, aren't you bored?" Qin Shanshan asked.

Chen Guiliang pointed to his English practice worksheet. "Which one should I choose for this?"

"B." Qin Shanshan's English was quite good. She gave the answer with a single glance.

Chen Guiliang asked, "Why B?"

Qin Shanshan said, "No reason, it's a fixed phrase."

Chen Guiliang took out a small notebook and jotted down the long-forgotten phrase.

"Are you pursuing Bian Guanyue?" Qin Shanshan asked.

Chen Guiliang smiled. "Guess."

Qin Shanshan just wanted to find something interesting to do. "Want me to help? I can ask her out on the weekend."

"Do you think I need help?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Qin Shanshan thought for a moment. "Doesn't seem like it. You two seem to have a pretty good relationship."

After saying that, she slumped back onto her desk, her mind wandering.

In senior year, there were always some people who fell into a state of confusion, aimlessly drifting through their days, not knowing what to do.

(While writing this chapter, I was suddenly reminded of an older lady.)

(She was a vocational school graduate. After her husband died in the line of duty, she returned to her hometown with her son. While her son was in middle school, she came to study in high school, hoping to fulfill her university dream. She hadn't touched a textbook in nearly twenty years, yet she got into Sichuan University in her first year, but didn't go. The second year, she came to audit our class and got into Zhejiang University!)

A vocational school graduate, son in middle school... she would have gotten into vocational school around 1983... damn, back then only the students with good grades went to vocational school. Because graduating from vocational school guaranteed a job assignment. For a kid from a rural family, earning money early meant finishing vocational school early, and upon entering a factory, you weren't a worker, but a cadre.
